title: GCSE Biology
intro: Exam-style questions on cells, organisation, disease, bioenergetics, homeostasis, inheritance and ecology.

questions.prompt: Which cell structure is the site of aerobic respiration?
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration takes place in the mitochondria, releasing energy from glucose for the cell to use.

questions.prompt: Which structure is found in bacterial cells but not in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotes. They have small rings of DNA called plasmids and no nucleus, while animal cells have a nucleus and no plasmids.

questions.prompt: In which cell structure are proteins made?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis. The nucleus holds the genetic code, but proteins are assembled on ribosomes.

questions.prompt: Under a microscope, an image of a cell is 10 mm across. The real cell is 0.02 mm across. What is the magnification?
questions.explanation: Magnification = image size ÷ real size, so 10 ÷ 0.02 = 500. Always use the same units for both sizes.

questions.prompt: How many genetically identical daughter cells does mitosis produce from one cell?
questions.explanation: Mitosis produces two daughter cells, each with the same chromosomes as the parent cell. It is used for growth and repair.

questions.prompt: What is the name for the diffusion of water from a dilute solution to a more concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane?
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the movement of water across a partially permeable membrane, from a dilute solution to a more concentrated one.

questions.prompt: Which process uses energy from respiration to move substances against a concentration gradient?
questions.explanation: Active transport moves substances from a low to a high concentration, so it needs energy from respiration. Root hair cells use it to absorb mineral ions.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme breaks down starch into sugars?
questions.explanation: Amylase is a carbohydrase that breaks starch down into sugars. It is made in the salivary glands, pancreas and small intestine.

questions.prompt: Which organ produces bile?
questions.explanation: Bile is made in the liver and stored in the gall bladder before it is released into the small intestine.

questions.prompt: Bile is an enzyme that breaks fats down into fatty acids and glycerol.
questions.explanation: Bile is not an enzyme. It emulsifies fats into small droplets, giving lipase a bigger surface area, and neutralises stomach acid.

questions.prompt: Which type of blood vessel has thick, muscular and elastic walls to cope with blood at high pressure?
questions.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart at high pressure, so they have thick layers of muscle and elastic fibres.

questions.prompt: The heart's natural pacemaker is a group of cells found in which chamber?
questions.explanation: The natural pacemaker sits in the wall of the right atrium and controls the resting heart rate.

questions.prompt: Which plant tissue transports dissolved sugars around the plant?
questions.explanation: Phloem carries dissolved sugars from the leaves to the rest of the plant. This movement is called translocation.

questions.prompt: What type of pathogen causes measles?
questions.explanation: Measles is a viral disease spread by droplets from sneezes and coughs. Most young children are vaccinated against it.

questions.prompt: Which disease is caused by a protist and spread by mosquitoes?
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by a protist. Mosquitoes act as vectors, carrying it from person to person.

questions.prompt: Antibiotics can be used to cure illnesses caused by viruses.
questions.explanation: Antibiotics kill bacteria but do not affect viruses, because viruses live and reproduce inside the body's own cells.

questions.prompt: The heart drug digitalis was first extracted from which plant?
questions.explanation: Digitalis comes from foxgloves. Aspirin, by contrast, was developed from a chemical found in willow bark.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a limiting factor for the rate of photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, temperature and the amount of chlorophyll can limit photosynthesis. Oxygen is a product, not a limiting factor.

questions.prompt: What is produced by anaerobic respiration in human muscle cells?
questions.explanation: Without enough oxygen, muscles break glucose down to lactic acid. This creates an oxygen debt that must be repaid afterwards.

questions.prompt: What are the products of anaerobic respiration in yeast cells?
questions.explanation: Yeast carries out fermentation, making ethanol and carbon dioxide. This is used in bread making and brewing.

questions.prompt: Which hormone, made by the pancreas, lowers blood glucose concentration?
questions.explanation: Insulin makes cells take in glucose and makes the liver and muscles store it as glycogen, so blood glucose falls.

questions.prompt: Which gland is often called the master gland because it controls many other glands?
questions.explanation: The pituitary gland in the brain releases hormones that cause other glands to release their own hormones.

questions.prompt: Which hormone, released by the thyroid gland, helps control the body's metabolic rate?
questions.explanation: Thyroxine from the thyroid gland stimulates the basal metabolic rate. It is controlled by negative feedback.

questions.prompt: Type 1 diabetes is caused by the pancreas producing too little insulin.
questions.explanation: In type 1 diabetes the pancreas makes little or no insulin, so it is usually treated with insulin injections.

questions.prompt: How many chromosomes are found in the nucleus of a normal human body cell?
questions.explanation: Human body cells have 23 pairs of chromosomes, making 46 in total. Gametes have 23.

questions.prompt: Two parents with the genotypes Bb and bb have a child. What is the probability the child has the genotype bb?
questions.explanation: A Punnett square gives Bb, Bb, bb and bb. Two out of four outcomes are bb, which is a probability of 50%.

questions.prompt: What term describes an organism that has two identical alleles for a gene?
questions.explanation: Homozygous means both alleles are the same, such as BB or bb. Heterozygous means they are different, such as Bb.

questions.prompt: A human male normally has the sex chromosomes XX.
questions.explanation: Males normally have XY sex chromosomes and females normally have XX.

questions.prompt: Which of these is an abiotic factor in an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Abiotic factors are non-living, such as soil pH, light intensity and temperature. The others are biotic, caused by living things.

questions.prompt: A field is 200 m². Quadrats show a mean of 3 daisies per m². Estimate the daisy population of the field.
questions.explanation: Population estimate = mean per m² × total area, so 3 × 200 = 600 daisies.
